logicalBugs.explanation: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. Enter the dashboard’s fullscreen mode and choose More info. No information dialog is visible until fullscreen is exited, when the already-open dialog appears; the button is not simply failing to receive the click.

rootCause.explanation: The dashboard enters element fullscreen while the info UI is mounted through a portal outside that element. The browser only presents descendants of the fullscreen element, so the already-open dialog appears after fullscreen exits.

reproductionPaths.explanation: In Metabase, a dashboard is a page of charts, tables and text. Enter its fullscreen mode and choose More info: no information dialog is visible. Exiting fullscreen reveals the already-open dialog, showing that the action ran but its result was hidden outside the fullscreen view.

sourceBugs.name: Dashboard info dialog stays hidden in fullscreen

reproductionPaths.expected: More info should display its dialog while the dashboard is in fullscreen mode.
reproductionPaths.actual: The More info control becomes ineffective in dashboard fullscreen mode because its dialog is not visible until fullscreen is closed.
reproSteps: Open a dashboard and enter fullscreen mode.
Select More info.
See no dialog in fullscreen, then exit fullscreen and see the dialog appear.

logicalBugs.explanation: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. On the supplied dashboard, choose a single product category and inspect the Product breakdown card. It continues showing every category despite the dashboard’s advertised filter; the report concerns this seeded card’s missing connection rather than a newly authored card that has never been mapped.

rootCause.explanation: Dashboard filtering applies only stored dashcard parameter_mappings. This card has no effective Product Category mapping in the seed; the application cannot infer a mapping from adjacent text or charts. Seed records need separate inspection.

reproductionPaths.explanation: On the supplied e-commerce dashboard, choose one product category in the dashboard filter, which should restrict its connected charts. The Product breakdown chart still includes every category even though surrounding text names the chosen one. This concerns the supplied chart’s missing filter connection, not a newly authored chart that was never connected.

sourceBugs.name: Product breakdown ignores the dashboard Product Category filter

reproductionPaths.expected: The breakdown should reflect the selected Product Category or clearly indicate that it is unfiltered.
reproductionPaths.actual: With Gizmo selected and surrounding copy naming Gizmo, Product breakdown still shows Doohickey, Gadget, Gizmo, and Widget percentages.
reproSteps: Open E-commerce Insights > Portfolio Performance.
Set Product Category to Gizmo only.
Compare the filter chip and adjacent Gizmo chart with Product breakdown, which still lists all four categories.

logicalBugs.explanation: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. Change the supplied dashboard’s date grouping from quarters to months. A revenue card updates to monthly values and comparison text but retains its quarterly title, so the saved heading misdescribes the currently displayed data.

rootCause.explanation: A saved card title is independent of the dashboard temporal-unit parameter. Changing grouping does not rewrite card names, so the seed title becomes misleading when Month is selected.

reproductionPaths.explanation: On the supplied dashboard, change Date Grouping from quarters to months. Its revenue chart updates the displayed period and comparison to months but keeps a quarterly title, so the heading no longer describes the chart’s current data.

sourceBugs.name: Revenue per quarter title remains after switching to monthly grouping

reproductionPaths.expected: The card title should reflect the selected Date Grouping.
reproductionPaths.actual: With Date Grouping set to Month, “Revenue per quarter” shows Sep 2026 and compares with the previous month.
reproSteps: Open E-commerce Insights on the Overview tab.
Set Date Grouping to Month.
Compare the Revenue per quarter title with its Sep 2026 and previous-month values.

logicalBugs.explanation: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. Open a filter’s selection checklist and reset the applied filter to its default. Results and applied values reset, but the still-open checklist keeps the previous selections instead of showing the values now in effect.

rootCause.explanation: The widget keeps selection in local draft state while dashboard reset updates the applied parameterValues. The open picker does not reinitialize its checked selections for that external reset.

reproductionPaths.explanation: On a dashboard, open a filter’s checklist of values and then use the filter’s reset-to-default action without closing that checklist. The applied selection and chart results reset, but the open checklist still checks only the previous values and offers Update filter. The draft choices therefore disagree with the restriction now applied to the dashboard.

sourceBugs.name: Resetting an open Product Category filter leaves stale checked options

reproductionPaths.expected: The open options should update to the default selections when the filter is reset.
reproductionPaths.actual: After resetting a Widget-only filter, the chip shows four selections while the open list still checks only Widget and offers Update filter.
reproSteps: On E-commerce Insights > Portfolio Performance, select only Widget in Product Category and apply.
Reopen the Product Category list, then click the chip’s Reset filter to default state control without closing the list.
Compare the four-selection chip with the stale Widget-only checklist.

logicalBugs.explanation: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. The supplied e-commerce example labels a section as customer satisfaction or customer survey responses, but its table contains wine/distillery reviews. This is unrelated seeded content under that advertised section, not a claim that users cannot place arbitrary content on their own dashboards.

rootCause.explanation: This is a seeded query/content mismatch: the survey card selects review bodies whose dataset concerns wine rather than the dashboard products. Rendering source only consumes the stored card query and rows.

reproductionPaths.explanation: The supplied e-commerce dashboard has a Customer Satisfaction section containing a Customer survey responses table. Its rows are wine and distillery reviews instead of feedback about the dashboard’s products or purchases. This is a mismatch in the supplied example content, not a restriction on what users may put on their own dashboards.

sourceBugs.name: Wine-tasting reviews shown in E-commerce Insights customer survey responses

reproductionPaths.expected: The Customer survey responses table under Customer Satisfaction should show feedback relevant to products or purchases in this e-commerce dashboard.
reproductionPaths.actual: The stable table shows reviews mentioning peachy fruit and 12-year-old bottlings, the Legacy series, a distillery, and distilling. This is inconsistent with the surrounding dashboard, which identifies product categories as Doohickey, Gizmo, Gadget, and Widget and lists items such as a Copper Knife, Silk Chair, Wool Car, and Keyboard as best sellers.
reproSteps: Sign in using the Metabase fixture account and open Examples → E-commerce Insights.
Select the Portfolio Performance tab.
Scroll to Customer Satisfaction → Customer survey responses.
Read the Body column. Observe sample reviews discussing whisky bottlings, the Legacy series, and distilleries.
Compare the review content with the dashboard’s displayed products and categories: Doohickey, Gizmo, Gadget, and Widget.

reproductionPaths.explanation: A Link card is a dashboard tile that navigates to another page. Save a dashboard containing external Link cards and duplicate the whole dashboard. The copy retains other cards and tabs but omits those Link cards entirely; duplicating an individual tab can preserve them, so the failure is specific to copying the whole dashboard.

logicalBugs.explanation: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. Turn off Auto-apply filters so viewers must click Apply before filter changes run, then duplicate the dashboard. The copy turns Auto-apply back on and immediately executes filter changes instead of retaining the source dashboard’s manual-apply behavior.

rootCause.explanation: The copy endpoint builds dashboard-data from an explicit whitelist of name, description, parameters, creator, collection, position and width; auto_apply_filters is omitted and takes its default.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Turn off Auto-apply filters on a dashboard so changing a filter stages the selection until Apply is clicked, then duplicate that dashboard. The copy has Auto-apply turned on and runs changes immediately instead of preserving the original’s manual-apply behavior. Both full duplication and the dashboard-only copy option exhibit this loss.

sourceBugs.name: Duplicating a dashboard re-enables disabled Auto-apply filters

reproductionPaths.expected: The duplicated dashboard preserves the source's saved Auto-apply filters setting and requires Apply when the source does.
reproductionPaths.actual: Both the full duplicate and 'Only duplicate dashboard' copy have Auto-apply filters enabled. Filter selection executes immediately in the copies, while the source stages changes until Apply.
reproSteps: Sign in and open a dashboard with a mapped filter, such as /dashboard/3-qa-dashboard-journeys.
Open the dashboard More menu, choose Edit settings, disable Auto-apply filters, and close settings.
Reopen the dashboard and verify Auto-apply filters remains disabled.
Choose More > Duplicate, enter a new name, and confirm Duplicate. Reproduce with either the default questions-copy mode or Only duplicate dashboard.
On the copied dashboard, open More > Edit settings. Observe Auto-apply filters is enabled.
Change a filter on the copy: queries execute immediately instead of waiting for Apply as they do on the source.

logicalBugs.explanation: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. Delete the selected tab, restore a revision from before that tab existed, or navigate Back to a removed tab. The remaining tabs still contain cards but none is selected, and the dashboard falsely says there is nothing there until the user manually chooses a surviving tab.

rootCause.explanation: useDashboardUrlQuery router listener parses nextLocation.query.tab and dispatches selectTab for any nonempty changed tab ID without checking that getTabs contains it. Thus a stale browser-history/URL tab can overwrite the reducer's repaired selectedTabId with a deleted ID and hide content.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Dashboard tabs divide a page’s charts and text into separate views. With a later-created tab selected, restore a saved revision from before that tab existed. The surviving tabs still contain content, but none becomes selected and the page says “There’s nothing here, yet” until the user chooses a remaining tab.

sourceBugs.name: Reverting dashboard history leaves a deleted tab selected and hides restored content

reproductionPaths.expected: When a history revert removes the active tab, the dashboard selects a surviving tab and displays its restored cards.
reproductionPaths.actual: Surviving tabs remain visible but none is selected; the dashboard displays 'There's nothing here, yet' with no grids. Clicking Tab 1 immediately restores its existing charts.
reproSteps: Sign in and open a saved dashboard with charts on Tab 1 and a history revision, such as /dashboard/8.
Enter Edit mode, create a new tab, add a heading such as QA Revert, and Save while the new tab is selected.
Click the Edited… history control and open History.
Revert to a revision from before the new tab existed (the reproduced entry on dashboard8 was 'You untrashed this Dashboard').
Close the info/history panel and wait for the restored dashboard to settle.
Observe that the remaining tabs are visible but no tab is selected, and the page says 'There's nothing here, yet'.
Click Tab 1; its restored charts appear, proving the empty state was incorrect.

reproductionPaths.explanation: On a dashboard with populated tabs, delete the tab that was selected when the page loaded, before clicking any tab manually. No remaining tab is selected, and the page shows its empty-dashboard message instead of the surviving charts. Clicking a tab before performing the deletion avoids this specific setup.

sourceBugs.name: Deleting the initially selected dashboard tab leaves no tab selected and hides the remaining tab's cards

reproductionPaths.expected: After deleting the active tab, select a remaining tab and display its existing content rather than showing the dashboard creation empty state.
reproductionPaths.actual: Delete the tab that was selected on load (URL ?tab= or default) before clicking any tab. No tab ends up selected and the dashboard shows the empty state while the remaining tab still has cards. Clicking a tab first works (control).
reproSteps: Dashboard 25 is an owned disposable fixture. Do not modify seeded dashboards or questions. Fresh two-tab fixture with saved content in both tabs is sufficient to test equivalent behavior.
Create a fresh QA-prefixed dashboard with two tabs named QA Source and QA Target.

Add text and a link to each tab; save and reload to verify both tabs contain their distinct content. Observed fixture had QA Source text “QA copied text — independent target 2026” plus a dashboard link.
Select second tab QA Target, enter Edit dashboard, open its tab dropdown and choose Delete.
Observe remaining QA Source tab and dashboard canvas without selecting another tab.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Visit a dashboard tab, delete that tab and save the dashboard, then use browser Back to return to the removed tab’s address. No surviving tab becomes selected and the page appears empty even though other tabs contain charts. It should recover to an existing tab or explain the missing destination.

sourceBugs.name: Browser Back to a deleted dashboard tab shows an empty dashboard with no tab selected

reproductionPaths.expected: Going back in browser history to a tab that was deleted falls back to an existing tab or says the tab is gone.
reproductionPaths.actual: After deleting a previously visited tab and saving, browser Back leaves no tab selected and shows There's nothing here, yet with Add a chart, although the remaining tabs have content.
reproSteps: Duplicate a dashboard that has several populated tabs.
Create an empty tab, save, and visit that tab.
Return to the first tab, edit the dashboard, delete the visited tab, and save.
Press browser Back and observe no tab is selected and the empty-dashboard placeholder shows.

logicalBugs.explanation: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. Give a dashboard filter both a default and “Always require a value”, then open its URL with an explicit empty value for that filter. The empty URL selection bypasses the required default and allows connected queries to run without the intended restriction.

rootCause.explanation: getParameterValueFromQueryParams returns null immediately for maybeParameterValue === empty string, before checking required/default. This URL-clearing branch therefore bypasses the required-value rule.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Give a dashboard filter a default and enable Always require a value, then open the dashboard address with that filter explicitly set to an empty URL value. The required filter becomes blank and its connected chart runs without the intended restriction instead of retaining a value or preventing execution. The same bypass is observed in the public dashboard view.

sourceBugs.name: Empty URL parameter bypasses a required dashboard filter

reproductionPaths.expected: A dashboard filter configured as required should keep a valid selection or prevent its mapped question from running without one; an empty URL parameter should not clear it and run unfiltered.
reproductionPaths.actual: A Region filter with default us-east and Always require a value returns two rows normally. Loading the dashboard with region= leaves the required filter blank and its mapped question returns all six rows, including in the public dashboard.
reproSteps: Create a dashboard with a question containing rows from multiple regions; add a Region filter and map it to the question.
Set default Region to us-east and enable Always require a value. Save the dashboard.
Open the saved dashboard and confirm Region shows us-east and the mapped question returns the two matching seeded rows.
Load the same dashboard URL with an empty region query parameter (region=), keeping other parameters unchanged. Wait for the page to settle.
Observe the Region chip is blank and the mapped question returns all six seeded rows; the required setting remains enabled.
If public sharing is available, open the public dashboard and repeat the control and empty-parameter navigations; observe the same two-to-six row change.

logicalBugs.explanation: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. Change a dashboard filter from several values to one, or connect it to a SQL variable that accepts only one value, then save. Previously selected extra values remain applied or sent to the query, producing multi-value results or a card error even when the configuration or visible chip now implies one value.

rootCause.explanation: A dashboard multi-value parameter is forwarded to a single-value native template tag without coercing the applied values to the target tag cardinality. Changing widget configuration also leaves already-applied multiple values intact.

reproductionPaths.explanation: A dashboard filter passes selected values into connected chart queries. Start with several selected values, then connect that filter to a saved SQL query’s plain-text input, which accepts only one value. Saving changes the visible control to single-value mode, but the query still receives multiple values and the chart fails; selecting just one value works.

sourceBugs.name: Mapping a multi-value filter to a SQL text variable keeps the extra values and breaks the card

reproductionPaths.expected: Mapping the Region filter to the card should filter the card and display results.
reproductionPaths.actual: With two Region values selected, map the dashboard filter to a SQL question's plain text variable and save. Metabase silently switches the filter to "A single value" and the chip shows one value, but the card query still sends both and the card shows "There was a problem displaying this chart." One selected value works (control).
reproSteps: Duplicate seeded Release overview dashboard using Only duplicate the dashboard and a unique QA name.
Edit the copy. Add Text or Category filter Region (Is), map Release requests table to Region, save. Select us-east and us-west and apply.
Edit copy, add Tab 2 and add existing saved question Release requests by region and category; save. The new card displays six rows before mapping.
Edit, select Region filter on Tab 2, choose Region in the card's Column to filter on dropdown. The settings automatically change from Dropdown list/Multiple values to Input box/A single value.
Click Done and Save.

reproductionPaths.explanation: On a dashboard with two values already applied in a filter, edit that filter from Multiple values to A single value and save. The filter still displays two selections and the charts continue aggregating both, instead of reducing the applied selection to match the new single-value configuration.

sourceBugs.name: Saving a filter configuration change from multiple values to a single value leaves two applied selections on the dashboard

reproductionPaths.expected: After changing a filter setting from 'Multiple values' to 'A single value' and saving the dashboard, the applied filter selection and card metrics should revalidate to a single value.
reproductionPaths.actual: After saving the dashboard, the filter bar still displays 'Vendor: 2 selections' and cards continue showing data aggregated across both vendors (Revenue per quarter remains 502.14 and Total orders remains 7).
reproSteps: As eval@momentic.ai, open E-commerce Insights dashboard1; ellipsis > Duplicate; choose Only duplicate the dashboard and give a unique disposable name.
Edit duplicate's Vendor filter. Select Multiple values, set default Alfreda Konopelski II Group, enable Always require a value, Done and Save.
In view mode select both Alfreda Konopelski II Group and Alfredo Kuhlman Group in Vendor and Update filter.
Edit Vendor again, select A single value, confirm default is Alfreda Konopelski II Group, Done and Save.
Observe Vendor and rendered results before refreshing. Then refresh to compare.

logicalBugs.explanation: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. Set a dashboard date filter to Before or After and choose a specific time as well as a date. Applying it discards the time component, so the connected cards use a date-only boundary rather than the one shown in the picker.

rootCause.explanation: Date parameter normalization/serialization uses the calendar-date operator representation rather than the full datetime endpoint, dropping time before the chart request.

reproductionPaths.explanation: A dashboard date filter limits the records used by connected charts. Choose Before or After and enter a specific hour as well as a date. The filter label and address retain that time, but chart results use a date-only boundary, wrongly excluding otherwise matching records later on the selected day. Other date operators and query-editor controls are separate paths.

sourceBugs.name: Dashboard After or Before date filters ignore the selected time

reproductionPaths.expected: After October 17 2026 7:34 PM includes ID4, created at 7:35 PM that day, along with IDs5 and 6.
reproductionPaths.actual: A dashboard Date filter set to After <date> <time> (e.g. After Oct 17 9:38 PM) hides rows later that same day. The chip and URL keep the time, but the SQL uses created_at >= the next midnight. On, Between, question-builder and native SQL filters keep minute precision (controls).
reproSteps: Open seed2 Release overview. Duplicate with a fresh QA-Date-prefixed name and check Only duplicate the dashboard.
Edit duplicate, Add a filter or parameter > Date picker. Map Release requests to Created At; Done and Save.
Open Date > Fixed date range > On. Set October 17, 2026, Add time, enter 19:35 (7:35 PM), and apply. Observe ID4 dated October17 7:35 PM.
Reopen Date, choose After, change time to 19:34 (7:34 PM), and Update filter.

logicalBugs.explanation: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. Change a filter default, remove the filter and discard, or save an unrelated filter-label edit after clearing its value. The active selection can adopt the canceled default, lose its prior value, or reinstate a cleared default, and may be remembered on later visits; editing default/configuration state unexpectedly changes the viewer’s applied filter.

rootCause.explanation: setParameterDefaultValue updates the parameter definition and immediately dispatches setParameterValue; edit cancellation restores the definition but not the applied/last-used parameter state.

reproductionPaths.explanation: In dashboard edit mode, change a filter’s default and then Cancel > Discard changes. The unsaved default nevertheless stays applied to the visible charts and is remembered on later visits. The saved default itself remains unchanged, so discarding configuration edits unexpectedly alters the viewer’s active selection.

sourceBugs.name: Discarding a filter default edit keeps the canceled value applied and remembers it

reproductionPaths.expected: Discarding changes restores the dashboard to its prior Month grouping rather than applying the canceled Day grouping.
reproductionPaths.actual: Change a filter default in edit mode, then Cancel → Discard changes. The canceled value stays applied and is saved as your last-used value, so it returns on fresh visits. The saved default is unchanged.
reproSteps: Dashboards-only. Do not edit underlying questions or seed dashboard. Observed duplicate dashboard/31; create a fresh equivalent duplicate.
Open seed1 E-commerce Insights dashboard; use its menu Duplicate, give a fresh QA-Date2-prefixed name and check Only duplicate the dashboard.
Edit the duplicate, select Date Grouping, set Default value to Month, click Done and Save. Reopen the dashboard without query parameters to verify Month and monthly chart.
Edit Date Grouping again; change Default value from Month to Day.
Click dashboard Cancel, then Discard changes in the confirmation dialog.
Inspect the dashboard grouping and charts.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Apply a dashboard filter so its connected chart shows only a subset of records. Enter edit mode, remove that filter, then Cancel > Discard changes. The filter control returns but its previous active value does not, leaving it blank and broadening the chart results instead of restoring the pre-edit view.

sourceBugs.name: Discarding a filter removal restores the filter but clears its active value

reproductionPaths.expected: Discard changes should restore both the removed filter definition and its previous active selection, leaving the view unchanged.
reproductionPaths.actual: A fresh dashboard copy filtered Release requests Category to Documentation showed three rows IDs1,3,5 and text=Documentation in the URL. After Edit > remove Text > Cancel > Discard changes, Text reappeared empty, URL became text=, and all six rows including Infrastructure were displayed. Reproduced on three fresh dashboards.
reproSteps: Sign in, open /dashboard/2, and duplicate it with Only duplicate the dashboard enabled.
Edit the copy and add a Text or Category filter. Map it to Release requests > Category, then Done and Save.
In view mode select Documentation in the Text filter and click Add filter. Confirm three rows remain.
Click Edit dashboard, click the Text filter, and choose Remove.
Click the top Cancel button, then Discard changes.
Observe that Text returns with no selected value and the table now shows all six rows.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Clear a dashboard filter that has a saved default, then enter edit mode and change only another filter’s label. Saving the unrelated label edit reapplies the first filter’s default and changes the chart results. The previously cleared selection should remain cleared because the edit did not intentionally change it.

sourceBugs.name: Saving an unrelated filter label restores a cleared filter default value and changes dashboard results

reproductionPaths.expected: Saving an edit to another filter's label retains the cleared QA Zip value and the 20-order result.
reproductionPaths.actual: QA Zip reverts to default '02139' and 'Total orders by product category' changes from 20 orders to 'No results!'.

Clear QA Zip using its X. The Total orders card shows 20 Gizmo orders. Reload and verify the empty Zip and 20 persist.
Edit dashboard, open QA Price, rename its label to QA Price Limit, then Done and Save.
Observe QA Zip and the mapped Total orders card.

logicalBugs.explanation: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. Configure an existing fixed Between date range, reopen its picker and click the already selected Between mode again. The selected endpoints are rewritten instead of the unchanged mode preserving the range.

rootCause.explanation: Date picker tab selection reconstructs an initial range even when the selected mode is already Between instead of preserving the current endpoints.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Apply a fixed Between date range to a dashboard filter and reopen its picker. Click the already-selected Between tab without choosing a different mode. The endpoint fields change to other dates even though the filter label and calendar highlight retain the original range, instead of an unchanged mode preserving its current endpoints.

sourceBugs.name: Re-clicking the selected Between tab rewrites the date range

reproductionPaths.expected: Clicking the selected Between tab preserves March 2 and March 3 bounds in the editor.
reproductionPaths.actual: With a dashboard Date Range filter applied as March 2–3, reopen it and click the already-selected Between tab. The fields change to January 31 – March 2 while the chip and calendar highlight still show March 2–3. Clicking another tab and back, or not clicking, keeps the range (control).
reproSteps: Observed on own dashboard/31. Fresh equivalent setup requested; Dashboards only. This followed Date Grouping restriction to Day/Week and switching Day to Week; uncertain whether grouping restriction is necessary.
Duplicate seed1 E-commerce Insights with Only duplicate the dashboard checked and a fresh QA-Date2-prefixed name.
Set Date Range Between March 2, 2026 and March 3, 2026 and apply.
Edit Date Grouping options to only Day and Week, save, then select Day. Refresh and select Week.
Open Date Range and click its already selected Between tab.
Compare Start/End editor fields against applied range chip and highlighted calendar dates.

logicalBugs.explanation: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. A required dashboard filter connected to a SQL variable can still be emptied through its text input. The UI permits the missing-required-value state instead of keeping a value or making its required status enforceable at that control.

rootCause.explanation: The native/text widget forwards an empty edited value without applying the required parameter default/validation used by the clear affordance.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Connect a dashboard filter to a saved SQL query’s text input, give it a default, and enable Always require a value. Its inline input can still be cleared using ordinary typing and submission gestures, leaving the required filter empty instead of preserving or restoring a usable value. This is the direct text-input path, separate from supplying an empty value in the page address.

sourceBugs.name: Required dashboard filter mapped to a SQL variable can be cleared from its text input

reproductionPaths.expected: A required filter should never be empty. Clearing it should either keep the previous value or reset it to the default, Documentation, so the category predicate stays applied.
reproductionPaths.actual: A required dashboard filter (with a default) mapped to a SQL text variable renders as an inline input. Clear it (Ctrl+A, Backspace) and press Enter, Tab or click away: the URL becomes category= and the card shows all rows. Popover widgets, a blur on an already-empty input, and the saved SQL question all restore the default (controls).
reproSteps: As an admin, duplicate the Release overview dashboard with Only duplicate the dashboard checked, and edit the copy.
Add the saved SQL question Release requests by region and category. Add a Text or Category filter and map it only to that card's Category variable.
Set the filter to Input box, A single value, default Documentation, and Always require a value. Save. The filter shows as an inline text box and the card shows the Documentation rows.
Type Infrastructure in the filter and press Enter. The card filters to Infrastructure.

logicalBugs.explanation: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. Open the fixed-date Between picker on a phone-width dashboard. Its calendars and controls extend beyond the viewport, leaving part of the range editor unavailable rather than fitting a usable mobile layout.

rootCause.explanation: The date picker renders its two-calendar/fixed-width range content without constraining it to available phone width.

reproductionPaths.explanation: At phone width, open a dashboard’s date filter and choose Fixed date range > Between. The two-calendar editor is wider than the screen: the end-date field and confirmation control extend beyond the viewport. The offered range picker therefore does not provide a fully visible, usable mobile layout.

sourceBugs.name: Fixed date range picker overflows the viewport on phones

reproductionPaths.expected: The date filter picker should fit the mobile viewport so both date fields and the confirmation control are visible.
reproductionPaths.actual: At phone width (390px), open a dashboard date filter → Fixed date range → Between. The two-calendar picker renders ~634px wide; the end date is clipped, Add filter sits off the right edge, and the page scrolls horizontally. Fits at 640px and wider; Before/On/After fit at 390 (controls).
reproSteps: Sign in and open /dashboard/1.
Set the browser viewport to 390×844 (or use a narrow mobile-sized window).
Click Date Range, then Fixed date range….

logicalBugs.explanation: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. Set a numeric Between filter with reversed endpoints and then reopen it. Swapping those values into valid order can leave Update disabled, while the default-value editor can accept a reversed pair without useful validation; distinguish the inability to correct the active filter from an empty result that is mathematically correct for reversed bounds.

rootCause.explanation: getUpdateButtonProps uses areParameterValuesIdentical for current/default/draft comparison. That helper sorts every array before comparing, treating ordered Between endpoints as an unordered selection: [100,50] equals [50,100], disabling a corrective update or labeling a reversed draft Set to default. NumberInputWidget also passes isValid unconditionally, so reversed ranges are not separately rejected.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Apply a numeric Between filter to a dashboard with its lower bound greater than its upper bound, producing the expected empty result. Reopen the picker and swap the endpoints into valid order. Update filter remains disabled, preventing the user from correcting and applying the now-valid range; the defect is correction being blocked, not the original empty result.

sourceBugs.name: Between number filter cannot be corrected from reversed bounds because Update filter stays disabled

reproductionPaths.expected: The 'Update filter' button remains enabled so the updated range from 100 to 300 can be submitted.
reproductionPaths.actual: Apply a Between number filter with reversed bounds (300, 100): No results, as expected. Reopen it and fix the order to 100, 300: Update filter stays disabled and Enter does nothing, so the empty dashboard can't be corrected. Any non-permuted change (100, 301) works (control).
reproSteps: Duplicate Release overview via dashboard menu; use a unique QA-Filter name and check Only duplicate the dashboard.
Edit owned copy; add Text or Category filter named Region, map Release requests to Region, save; select us-east and us-west and apply.
Edit owned copy; add Number filter named Amount, map Release requests to Amount, choose Between operator, save.
Set Amount range 120 to 240 and apply; verify rows 1 and 2. Change to 120.5 to 240.5 and apply; verify only row 2.
Change Amount to 300 to 100 and apply; dashboard shows No results. Refresh and reopen Amount.
Correct first endpoint to 100 and second to 300. Attempt Update filter.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Give a dashboard’s numeric Between filter a valid saved default range. Later enter those endpoints in reverse order: the button changes to Set to default, but clicking it applies the reversed values rather than restoring the configured default. The chart then shows no results and reopening retains the inverted range, contradicting the offered reset action.

sourceBugs.name: Number Between filter changes button to 'Set to default' for reversed default endpoints and applies the reversed range without validation

reproductionPaths.expected: Entering range endpoints or resetting to default should restore or enforce the configured ordered range (10.25 and 50.75) rather than applying an inverted range.
reproductionPaths.actual: Entering 50.75 and 10.25 changes the button to 'Set to default', which applies the reversed range, leaves the chart showing 'No results!', and retains the reversed inputs upon reopening.
reproSteps: Create a disposable copy of E-commerce dashboard, edit it and add Number filter named QA Price.
Select Between operator, connect Total orders by product category to PRODUCT Price, and set default range to 10.25 then 50.75. Done and Save.
Open QA Price in dashboard view, enter -10.25 and -0.75 and Update filter.
Reopen filter, enter 50.75 in first field and 10.25 in second. The action is labeled Set to default.
Click Set to default and reopen QA Price.

logicalBugs.explanation: Dashboard text and heading cards render authored Markdown, which can include lists, links and variables whose values come from connected dashboard filters. Set a text card’s horizontal alignment to Center while its content is a Markdown bullet list. The text is centered but bullet markers remain at the left edge, so the list items and their markers do not align together.

rootCause.explanation: Text applies text-align:center to the Markdown container while list-item markers remain outside their content box under standard list styling; marker positioning is not changed with alignment.

reproductionPaths.explanation: A dashboard text card is a tile that renders Markdown formatting. Fill it with a bullet list and choose Center horizontal alignment. The item text becomes centered but the bullet markers remain at the card’s left edge instead of aligning beside their items.

sourceBugs.name: Center-aligned text card leaves Markdown bullet markers at the left edge

reproductionPaths.expected: With Horizontal Alignment set to Center, list bullets stay next to their item text.
reproductionPaths.actual: The list item text is centered while the bullet markers stay at the left edge of the card.
reproSteps: Edit a dashboard and add a Text card with a heading and two bullet list items.
Open the card's visualization options and set Horizontal Alignment to Center.
Save and observe the bullets are detached from the centered text.

logicalBugs.explanation: Dashboard text and heading cards render authored Markdown, which can include lists, links and variables whose values come from connected dashboard filters. Use Middle or Bottom vertical alignment in a text card whose content exceeds its height. Earlier lines overflow above the scroll origin and cannot be reached by ordinary scrolling instead of remaining accessible within the card.

rootCause.explanation: Text applies justify-center/justify-end on a flex-column Markdown container even when its content exceeds available height, positioning overflow before scrollTop=0 and making the top unreachable.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Put more text in a dashboard text card than fits its height, then choose Middle or Bottom vertical alignment. Earlier lines are positioned above the scrollable area and cannot be reached by normal scrolling. The problem is inaccessible overflowed content, rather than text merely starting below the top of the card.

sourceBugs.name: Bottom- or middle-aligned text cards hide overflowing content above the scroll area

reproductionPaths.expected: All text remains readable by scrolling within the card; when content exceeds card height, alignment should not put it outside the scrollable bounds.
reproductionPaths.actual: A dashboard text card with more content than fits, set to Vertical Alignment Bottom, shows only the end of its text. The heading and list sit above the scroll area and can't be scrolled to. The same card set to Top scrolls through everything; a taller Bottom card shows all content (controls).
reproSteps: From /collection/root, create a new dashboard. Add a Text card.

Enter this multiline Markdown: “# Text dashboard”, a blank line, “- First item”, “- Second item”, a blank line, “[Internal link](/dashboard/2)”, a blank line, “| Name | Value |”, “|---|---|”, and “| Test | 42 |”. Keep the default short text-card height.
Open the text card’s Show visualization options. Set Vertical Alignment to Bottom, click Done, and save the dashboard.
Reload and try to read the beginning of the card by scrolling. The heading and list are inaccessible; only the final content is visible.
As a control, change Vertical Alignment to Top: the heading appears and the card provides a scrollbar for the rest.

logicalBugs.explanation: Dashboard cards have visualization settings for chart type, colors, axes and number formatting; a custom click action can navigate to a URL or change dashboard filters. Use Reset to defaults while editing a dashboard card’s visualization. Canceling afterward can retain the reset instead of undoing that draft operation, while a progress-card color changed in the same editor can fail to reset at all; both involve the reset action disagreeing with the editor’s visible settings or commit/cancel boundary.

rootCause.explanation: Visualization reset changes settings through the parent update path rather than keeping an independent complete draft/snapshot, so closing with Cancel cannot restore all previous settings, including progress color.

reproductionPaths.explanation: On a dashboard table card, save formatting and pagination settings, then reopen its visualization editor and choose Reset to defaults. Cancel that editor, or dismiss it with Escape. The reset remains applied to the card instead of cancellation preserving its previously saved appearance and table behavior.

sourceBugs.name: Cancel does not undo Reset to defaults in dashboard card visualization settings

reproductionPaths.expected: Clicking Cancel should discard the reset and preserve the previously saved table formatting and pagination settings.
reproductionPaths.actual: In dashboard edit mode, open a card's visualization settings, click Reset to defaults, then Cancel (or Escape). The card loses its conditional formatting, pagination and custom title anyway. Other edits made in the same modal are discarded by Cancel (control).
reproSteps: Create an isolated dashboard copy of Release overview with an existing Release requests table; do not alter the seed or question.

Edit the table visualization: enable pagination and add whole-row Region = us-east blue and Amount > 200 green conditional rules. Save visualization and dashboard, then refresh to verify colors and pagination.
Edit dashboard, open Release requests visualization options, click Reset to defaults, then Cancel.
Observe the card and reopen visualization options.

reproductionPaths.explanation: A dashboard progress card shows a value against a goal using a colored bar. In its visualization editor, change the bar color and then choose Reset to defaults. Both the color swatch and preview remain on the changed color instead of restoring the default, so the reset does not undo that draft setting.

sourceBugs.name: Reset to defaults keeps a changed progress card color

reproductionPaths.expected: Reset to defaults puts the progress visualization back to its default settings, so the color returns to the original green (#88BF4D).
reproductionPaths.actual: After Reset to defaults, the Color swatch and the preview bar stay red (#E75454). Nothing visible changes and there is no feedback.
reproSteps: As an admin, open the seeded E-commerce Insights dashboard.
Open the header ... menu, click Duplicate, set the name to 'QA Reset Color 7731', tick 'Only duplicate the dashboard', and click Duplicate.
Click Edit dashboard (pencil). Hover the 'Revenue goal for this quarter' card and click Show visualization options.
On the Display tab, click the green Color swatch and choose red (#E75454). The preview turns red.
Click Reset to defaults and wait 5 seconds. The swatch and bar are still red.

logicalBugs.explanation: Dashboard cards have visualization settings for chart type, colors, axes and number formatting; a custom click action can navigate to a URL or change dashboard filters. Configure a card’s custom click destination, then change an unrelated visualization setting and save. rootCause.explanation: Dashcard visualization settings save replaces the settings object without preserving the separate click_behavior entry, falling back to default drill-through.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Configure a dashboard chart so clicking it performs a custom action, such as updating a connected filter. Change an unrelated visualization option or title and save. Clicking the chart now opens its ordinary drill-through menu instead of the previously configured action, so editing appearance discards navigation/filter behavior.

sourceBugs.name: Changing a dashboard card's visualization settings resets its click behavior to drill-through

reproductionPaths.expected: Changing a card's display settings, such as Show total or its title, keeps the card's configured click behavior.
reproductionPaths.actual: A donut card set to Update a dashboard filter on click reverts to Open the drill-through menu after a visualization setting is changed and saved.
reproSteps: Duplicate a dashboard with a donut chart card.
Edit the card's click behavior to Update a dashboard filter and map a column to a filter; save.
Edit the dashboard, open the card's visualization settings, change Show total, and save.
Reopen click behavior and observe it is back to the drill-through menu.

logicalBugs.explanation: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. Change the dashboard’s title to spaces only. Inline editing leaves a blank header until reload even though the save was rejected; the full edit form instead reports “Save failed” without explaining the invalid name. An exactly empty title that correctly restores the prior name is not the same failure.

rootCause.explanation: Dashboard title editing/submission checks raw nonempty input instead of trimmed content; the API rejects the nonblank name contract but the inline/editor state is not restored or explained.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Rename a dashboard inline to spaces only and finish the edit by clicking away or pressing Enter. The title remains visibly blank without an error, even though the server rejected the rename and reloading restores the previous saved title. This is a misleading unsaved header, not a successfully stored blank name.

sourceBugs.name: Whitespace-only inline dashboard rename leaves a blank title with no error

reproductionPaths.expected: An invalid whitespace-only rename should immediately retain/revert to the last saved name or display validation, rather than leaving an apparently updated blank dashboard title.
reproductionPaths.actual: Rename a dashboard inline to only spaces and click away (or press Enter). The title goes blank with no error; the server rejected the save (400) and a reload restores the old name. An empty rename reverts correctly and valid renames save (controls).
reproSteps: Use a fresh owned dashboard; do not mutate shared seeds or questions. This is a missing invalid-input recovery/feedback issue, not a claim that blank names persist.
As Harbor Admin create a fresh disposable dashboard with a nonblank name, or duplicate a seeded dashboard into your own fixture. Observed fixture was dashboard 30 named QA-Life2 SearchRenamed-2030.
In saved view click the editable dashboard title and replace its entire contents with three spaces.
Click a dashboard content heading outside the title and wait for the settled state.
Observe blank title and no validation; reload the dashboard and compare.

reproductionPaths.explanation: In the full dashboard editor, replace the title with spaces only and click Save. The editor stays open and briefly says Save failed, but gives no explanation that the title is invalid. The missing validation feedback leaves the user unable to identify why this particular save was rejected.

sourceBugs.name: Saving a whitespace-only dashboard title fails and leaves the editor open without an explanatory validation message

reproductionPaths.expected: Reject the blank/whitespace title with an explanatory validation error indicating that the dashboard name cannot be blank.
reproductionPaths.actual: Clicking Save briefly changes the button text to 'Save failed' and leaves the editor open, without displaying any explanation or validation feedback.
reproSteps: Create a fresh uniquely named QA-Lifecycle dashboard using New > Dashboard, then save it.
Open Edit dashboard, replace the title with three spaces, and click Save.
Observe the editor after the attempted save.

logicalBugs.explanation: Global search finds saved questions, dashboards, models and metrics, and can restrict results by content type, date or whether an item is in Trash. Permanently delete a dashboard, then search with “Search items in trash” enabled. The deleted dashboard still appears as a result whose link opens a not-found page, rather than disappearing from search once it no longer exists.

rootCause.explanation: Search result indexing/invalidation outlives the deleted dashboard entity; clicking the stale hit requests a removed dashboard and produces Not found.

reproductionPaths.explanation: A dashboard is a saved page of charts and text that may first be moved to Trash. Permanently delete one, then use global search with Search items in trash enabled. The dashboard still appears, but its result opens Page Not Found instead of disappearing once the underlying item is permanently gone.

sourceBugs.name: Opening a permanently deleted dashboard from trash search shows a not-found page

reproductionPaths.expected: A dashboard search result opens the dashboard or its trash page, and permanently deleted items no longer appear.
reproductionPaths.actual: After permanently deleting a dashboard, searching with Search items in trash still lists it, and clicking the result opens the page-not-found screen.
reproSteps: Create a dashboard with a unique name and save it.
Move it to Trash, then delete it permanently from Trash.
Search for its name, open View and filter all results, and enable Search items in trash.
Click the dashboard result and observe the not-found page.

logicalBugs.explanation: Questions are saved queries, models are reusable table-like queries and metrics are saved aggregate calculations. Each has a title, a collection location and revision history. Opening History on a dashboard, model or metric can show “undefined modified this” where the person’s name should be. The observable failure is the literal missing-name text in an existing revision entry, not the absence of history or a claim that an unauthorized actor edited the item.

rootCause.explanation: Timeline revision copy reads r.user.common_name directly for another actor, without reconstructing a name or providing a fallback when the seeded revision user lacks that property.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Open More info > History on an existing dashboard. A saved revision entry reads “undefined modified this” where the editing person’s name should appear. This concerns the literal missing-name text in an available history entry, not missing revisions or evidence of an unauthorized edit.

sourceBugs.name: Sample dashboard History shows undefined as the author

reproductionPaths.expected: Every dashboard History entry names who made the change.
reproductionPaths.actual: On the sample E-commerce Insights dashboard, More info > History shows undefined modified this. A newly created dashboard shows You created this.
reproSteps: Open the sample E-commerce Insights dashboard.
Open More info > History.
Observe the entry reads undefined modified this.

logicalBugs.explanation: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. Configure a filter embedded inside a card with a default and “Always require a value”, then duplicate that card. The copied local filter loses its default or required-value choice instead of carrying those settings with the copied card.

rootCause.explanation: duplicateParameters passes _.omit(parameter,"id") into createParameter, but createParameter constructs a fresh object containing only id, name, slug, type and sectionId. Default, required, widget/source configuration and other inline options are discarded.

reproductionPaths.explanation: A dashboard card can have its own embedded filter rather than using a page-wide control. Give that local numeric filter a default range and enable Always require a value, then duplicate the card. The copy loses the default and required setting and can show rows outside the source range instead of preserving the local filter configuration.

sourceBugs.name: Duplicating a card drops its local filter default and required-value setting

reproductionPaths.expected: A duplicated card should retain its local filter configuration, including default values and Always require a value, and initially display the same filtered data.
reproductionPaths.actual: A Release requests card with a card-local Number Between Amount filter defaulted to 100–200 and required enabled duplicates with Number 1 set to No default and required disabled. The copy consequently displays rows outside the source's range (Amount 360 appeared alongside 120 in the tested Region subset). Reproduced twice.
reproSteps: Sign in, open /dashboard/2, and use Move, trash, and more… > Duplicate with Only duplicate the dashboard checked to create a test copy.
Edit the copy. Add a filter or parameter > Number > Between, and map it to Release requests > Amount.
Set its default range to 100 and 200, enable Always require a value, and move the filter onto the Release requests card. Click Done and Save.
Re-enter Edit dashboard, hover the Release requests card, choose Duplicate, and Save.
Compare the original and duplicated card data and local filters. Open the copied filter's editor: its default is missing and Always require a value is off.

logicalBugs.explanation: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. Create a tab containing filters embedded in text/heading cards and connected question cards, then duplicate the tab. Copied text can show raw variable syntax, opening a copied filter can jump to the original tab, or copied questions can ignore the displayed selection and show unfiltered totals; the copied controls and their card connections no longer describe the same tab.

rootCause.explanation: duplicateTab copies sourceDashCard by spread and replaces only id/dashboard_tab_id/isDirty. It does not clone dashboard parameters or rewrite inline parameter ownership and text mappings to the new card/tab.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Create a dashboard tab with a heading and text tile whose variable placeholders both display the value from a filter embedded in the heading. Duplicate the tab and save. The copied heading still shows the chosen value, but the copied text tile displays its raw placeholder even after reload, instead of retaining the same connection.

sourceBugs.name: Duplicating a tab loses text-card variable mappings

reproductionPaths.expected: Copied text cards should retain their mapped variables and display the same filter values as the original tab.
reproductionPaths.actual: A fresh dashboard contained Heading {{region}} and Text {{region}}, both mapped to a heading-local Region input filter default West, required enabled. Original rendered Heading West and Text West. Duplicating Tab1 produced Heading West but Text {{region}} in Copy of Tab1, persisting after full reload. Add a heading card with Heading {{region}}.

Set default West and enable Always require a value, then Done.
Add a text card with Text {{region}}. Click the heading's Region widget in Edit, map the text card's Select variable control to region, then Done and Save.
Verify both cards display West.
Edit dashboard, open Tab 1's dropdown, choose Duplicate, and Save.
View Copy of Tab 1 and reload: heading displays West, but the text displays literal {{region}}.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Duplicate a dashboard tab containing a heading with its own embedded text filter, then save and re-enter edit mode on the copied tab. Clicking the copied heading’s filter jumps selection and the address back to the original tab and opens its settings there. The user cannot configure the copied control in place.

sourceBugs.name: Editing a copied tab's card-local filter jumps to the original tab

reproductionPaths.expected: Clicking a card-local filter on the copied tab should keep that tab selected and configure the copied heading's filter.
reproductionPaths.actual: With Copy of Tab 1 selected in dashboard edit mode, clicking its heading's Text widget switches selection and URL to source Tab 1 and opens settings there. Reproduced on a fresh dashboard and reconfirmed after fresh navigation. fresh-navigation snapshots 16:57:44 and 16:57:49 show dashboard3 tab=24-copy-of-tab-1 switching to tab=10-tab-1.

Add a heading containing “Region {{region}}”. Hover the heading and choose Add a filter > Text or Category.
In the heading's Select… mapping choose region; set How should people filter to Input box, then Done and Save.
Edit the dashboard. Open Tab 1's chevron menu and choose Duplicate, then Save.

reproductionPaths.expected: Duplicating a tab should preserve the filter connections between its copied inline filter/heading and copied question cards, yielding the same filtered results as the source tab.

Select Gizmo and apply. The heading says Selected Gizmo and Revenue per quarter shows 15,576.4.
Edit, open the second tab's dropdown, choose Duplicate, then Save.

On the copied tab observe Selected Gizmo and the Gizmo filter, but Revenue per quarter shows 67,863.4. Reloading or selecting Widget does not fix the card. Existing reproduction: /dashboard/4?qa_category=Gizmo&tab=17.
reproductionPaths.explanation: Connect a filter embedded in a dashboard heading to both that heading’s text variable and a chart’s product-category field, then duplicate the tab. On the copy, the heading and filter still name the chosen category, but the chart shows totals across all categories and ignores further selection changes. The copied chart lost a connection that the copied controls still advertise.

sourceBugs.name: Duplicating tab disconnects question cards from inline filters

logicalBugs.explanation: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. A member opens More info for a dashboard created by another authorized user. “Creator and last editor” omits the creator row even though the dashboard has a valid creator, rather than displaying that person’s identity.

rootCause.explanation: DashboardDetails fetches the creator with useGetUserQuery(dashboard.creator_id) and renders the entire creator row only when creator exists. A member denied that user-detail endpoint sees no creator fallback even though the dashboard itself is readable.

reproductionPaths.explanation: As a member who can view a dashboard created by another user, open More info and inspect Creator and last editor. The last editor appears but the creator row is missing even though History identifies a valid creator. The failure is the omitted creator information, not absence of all dashboard metadata.

sourceBugs.name: Dashboard More info "Creator and last editor" omits creator row for Harbor Admin-created dashboard viewed by Maya

reproductionPaths.expected: The Creator and last editor card names Harbor Admin as the creator and Maya Chen as the last editor.
reproductionPaths.actual: The card shows only the last-editor row for Maya Chen. No creator row appears, even though History lists "Harbor Admin created this."
reproSteps: As an administrator, create the QA Collaboration dashboard in Our analytics with the description 'Admin-owned member edit baseline', add the existing Release requests card and save.

Open the History tab. It shows 'Harbor Admin created this.'

logicalBugs.explanation: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. Open the editor for an existing internal Metabase link card and save it without intentionally changing its target. The stored destination becomes malformed or points to the wrong location, so merely editing the card damages a link that previously worked.

rootCause.explanation: LinkViz editor parses a saved internal URL into entity/link state and serializes it back with a different destination representation, even when the user makes no change.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Save a dashboard Link card targeting another Metabase page, then open its pencil editor and save without changing the target. The link becomes malformed or points to the wrong place instead of preserving the previously working internal destination. Merely revisiting and confirming the editor damages the saved link.

sourceBugs.name: Opening an internal link card’s editor corrupts its destination when saved

reproductionPaths.expected: Opening the link editor and saving an unchanged card should preserve the selected dashboard target.
reproductionPaths.actual: A link selected from search initially points to /dashboard/2-release-overview. After opening its pencil editor and saving without edits, the href becomes literal 'Release overview'. It persists after reload, and clicking navigates to /Release%20overview with 'We're a little lost… The page you asked for couldn't be found.' Independently reproduced on dashboards4 and12.
reproSteps: Sign in and create a new dashboard through /collection/root > New > Dashboard.
In the editor choose Add a link or iframe > Link.
Type Release overview and select the existing dashboard from the search results. Save the dashboard.
Verify the link card opens or points to /dashboard/2-release-overview, then return to the test dashboard.
Click Edit dashboard, hover the internal link card, and click its pencil editor.
Without changing the input or selecting another result, click the dashboard Save button.

logicalBugs.explanation: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. Apply a numeric Between filter with its lower endpoint empty and only an upper endpoint entered. After reload, that upper value moves into the lower field and reverses the predicate from “at most” to “at least”; the lower field may have been left empty intentionally or cleared by invalid text.

rootCause.explanation: The approximate public source deserializeNumberParameterValue explicitly preserves a two-item [null,upper] array for number/between. Endpoint position must therefore be lost earlier in URL/value transport or the actual runtime implementation; this parser alone does not establish the root.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Apply a dashboard’s numeric Between filter with only an upper bound, leaving the lower field intentionally empty. Reload the dashboard. The upper value moves into the lower field and results change from “at most this value” to “at least this value,” rather than preserving the accepted one-sided range.

sourceBugs.name: Valid upper-only Between filter reverses to lower-only after reload

reproductionPaths.expected: Accepted upper-only range remains Amount <=240 after reload, retaining IDs 2 and 6.
reproductionPaths.actual: Reload changes results to IDs 2 and 4 (240 and 360), interpreting 240 as the lower bound instead. No invalid text was entered in this reproduction.
reproSteps: Create a dashboard with the Release requests card, a Number Between filter mapped to Amount, and a Boolean Approved filter set to False.
Open Amount; leave first bound empty and enter 240 in second bound. Add filter is enabled; apply it.
Observe Release requests IDs 2 and 6, amounts 240 and 150.
Reload the dashboard and inspect the same card.

matchingGuidance.claimScope: Credit any Between filter whose upper bound moves into the lower field after reload, whatever the reason the lower bound was empty, including invalid non-numeric input. Non-numeric input that clears a filter without the bound moving is a separate known-invalid reference.

logicalBugs.explanation: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. Open an empty dashboard while it is in Trash. It still offers Add a chart, leading users into an edit that fails with a permission error when saved instead of hiding or explaining the unavailable action.

rootCause.explanation: The empty dashboard state chooses its creation action from edit capability without also checking archived state, allowing an invalid edit/save flow on a trashed dashboard.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Move an empty dashboard to Trash and open it there. It still offers Add a chart and permits entering the editor, but adding a chart and saving ends on a permission-denied page. Reload confirms nothing was saved, so the interface offers an edit flow that cannot finish while the dashboard remains trashed.

logicalBugs.explanation: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. Configure a custom filter choice whose displayed label maps to an empty stored value, then select it and refresh. The selected custom label disappears or resets instead of surviving as the configured empty-value choice.

rootCause.explanation: Parameter URL parsing treats an empty raw string as null/cleared, so a selected display label whose actual value is empty cannot round-trip as a selection.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Configure a dashboard filter’s custom list with a visible label whose underlying value is empty. Select that label alongside other choices and apply it; the selection count includes it. After refresh, the empty-valued choice disappears and the count drops instead of preserving or rejecting that configured choice explicitly.

sourceBugs.name: Selecting a custom filter label configured with an empty raw value resets after page refresh

reproductionPaths.expected: Applying a selected custom list label should persist after a page refresh, or empty raw values should be disallowed.
reproductionPaths.actual: Selecting 'Orphan label' and applying the filter updates the count to 3 selections, but refreshing the page reverts the filter back to 2 selections.
reproSteps: Duplicate seed dashboard using ellipsis > Duplicate > Only duplicate dashboard and give the copy a unique name.
On the copy, edit dashboard > Product Category > selectable values Edit > Custom list. Enter exactly `, Orphan label`; click dialog Done, sidebar Done and Save.
Open Product Category. Leave two existing categories selected, select Orphan label, then Update filter.
Observe 3 selections, then refresh. Observe 2 selections; the empty-value selection is lost.

logicalBugs.explanation: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. Edit only the dashboard title or description, or trash it, and inspect History. It can also claim a pin-position, card or tab modification that the user did not make, especially on the first edit after reverting a revision; this is misleading change narration rather than the cards actually being edited in that operation.

rootCause.explanation: Dashboard revision serialization/restoration retains normalized positional/card/tab metadata; subsequent rename/edit diff compares different snapshots and reports those non-user edits as changes.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Duplicate a dashboard in a collection containing pinned dashboard shortcuts, so the operation changes the surrounding pin positions. On the copy, change only its title and inspect History. The entry also claims a pin-position change, although the rename itself did not change its position.

reproductionPaths.expected: A title-only rename records only the rename in History.
reproductionPaths.actual: History reads renamed this Dashboard … and changed pin position after only the title was edited.
reproSteps: Open a dashboard in a collection that has pinned dashboards and choose Duplicate > Only duplicate the dashboard, so the copy shifts the existing pin positions.
On the copy, rename the dashboard inline, changing only its title.
Reload, open More info > History, and read the latest entry: it also claims a pin-position change.

reproductionPaths.explanation: On a dashboard, remove a chart or tab and save, then use History to restore the revision that brings it back. Make a subsequent title-only, description-only or trash change. The first history entry after restoration also claims that cards or tabs were modified even though their visible arrangement stayed unchanged.

sourceBugs.name: After a History revert restores removed cards or tabs, the next dashboard edit is falsely recorded as modifying cards and tabs

reproductionPaths.expected: History describes only the change made (e.g. trashed, renamed, or edited the description), with no claim of card or tab edits.
reproductionPaths.actual: History shows e.g. 'trashed this Dashboard and modified the cards.' or a description edit that also modified the cards and tabs. Cards and tabs are visibly unchanged. Happens once, on the first edit after the revert.
reproSteps: Duplicate a seeded dashboard with Only duplicate the dashboard checked, and open the copy.
Edit the copy, remove one card, and save.
Open More info > History and revert to the revision before the card was removed, so the card comes back.
Make one more change: rename the dashboard, edit its description, or move it to trash.
Reload and open More info > History. The latest entry claims the change also modified the cards (or tabs), though they are unchanged.

logicalBugs.explanation: Global search finds saved questions, dashboards, models and metrics, and can restrict results by content type, date or whether an item is in Trash. Use Creation date’s “Before” search filter with a selected calendar date. Results still include items created on that very day, rather than only earlier days; this is the exclusive-boundary error even when the item’s displayed timezone/day is otherwise consistent.

rootCause.explanation: The absolute ~date decoder returns the selected date as :end. Search requests date-string->range with inclusive-end? false, whose adjust-inclusive-range-if-needed adds one day to the end; search then compares timestamp-date < that advanced bound. This makes Before include the selected day. The conversion must distinguish an already-exclusive Before endpoint from an inclusive range endpoint.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Create a dashboard and verify its creation date, then search for it using the Creation date filter’s Before operator with that same date. It remains in the results, just as it does under On that date, instead of being excluded by an exclusive “before” boundary. This is separate from a timezone disagreement about which day it was created.

reproductionPaths.actual: Before October 22, 2026 returns all four same-day QA-Maya dashboards. On October 22 also returned four, and Before October 21 returned none. The displayed Before filter therefore includes its selected date.

Select Creation date > Fixed date range > Before. Enter today's date (October 22, 2026 in this run) and Apply.
Observe that the newly created dashboard still appears; choosing the preceding date excludes it.

logicalBugs.explanation: Column and chart formatting control how numbers are displayed, including decimal places, currency labels and custom prefixes; these controls should represent the saved display settings. rootCause.explanation: The shared decimals setting has only nonnegative/integer checks and no formatter maximum. Values above the supported precision range reach scalar/gauge/pie number formatters, producing warnings or fallback integer/zero labels.

reproductionPaths.explanation: On a dashboard card displaying a single number, enter an unsupported very large decimal-place count, such as 101, in formatting settings and save. Click Done, save dashboard, and refresh.

logicalBugs.explanation: Global search finds saved questions, dashboards, models and metrics, and can restrict results by content type, date or whether an item is in Trash. Search by Creation date or Last edit using Today or a fixed calendar day and compare the results with the item’s displayed dates. Recently created or edited items can be excluded from Today, and fixed-date and relative-date choices can disagree; reported scope includes models, metrics, questions and seeded items never edited since creation. A browser/server midnight boundary is one observed trigger, not evidence that every matching report must establish a timezone diagnosis.

rootCause.explanation: Search date-range-filter-clause calls date-string->range without a viewer timezone. Relative decoding obtains t/local-date-time on the server, while the search comparison casts stored timestamps to date; browser-local date picks and previews therefore need not describe the same day near a timezone boundary. Exact fixture timezone configuration remains a prerequisite of each report. Seeded or never-edited item variants are now accepted by the source matching scope; the supplied evidence does not establish that each such exclusion has the same timezone cause rather than missing last-edit metadata. Attribution of those broader symptoms remains provisional.

logicalBugs.explanation: Dashboard text and heading cards render authored Markdown, which can include lists, links and variables whose values come from connected dashboard filters. Place a filter variable inside a Markdown link in a text card, then apply a value containing spaces. The rendered card shows raw link syntax rather than a clickable link because the substituted URL is not kept valid.

rootCause.explanation: fillParametersInText supports urlEncode but defaults it to false. Text calls it with escapeMarkdown:true and never enables urlEncode, so spaces in substituted filter values remain literal spaces in Markdown destinations and invalidate the link syntax.

reproductionPaths.explanation: A dashboard text tile can render a Markdown link containing a variable connected to a filter. The tile displays the raw Markdown link syntax instead of a clickable link, so inserting the selected value breaks an otherwise valid destination.

sourceBugs.name: Text-card Markdown link becomes raw, non-clickable syntax when mapped filter value contains spaces

reproductionPaths.expected: Mapped filter substitution in a working Markdown link should preserve an actionable link when the selected value contains spaces and special characters.

Set filter to Alpha: text substitutes Alpha and link is clickable; following it retains the selected filter.

logicalBugs.explanation: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. Visit multiple dashboard tabs, use browser Back, and change a filter on the restored tab. Browser Forward no longer restores the subsequently visited tab and its filter selection, even though changing that filter should not destroy the existing forward destination.

rootCause.explanation: useDashboardUrlQuery listens to browser navigation and dispatches selectTab when the URL tab changes. A separate effect treats the resulting queryParams.tab change as a new user tab change and dispatches push, creating a new entry after Back and clearing the previous Forward history.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Visit several tabs of a dashboard and choose filter values, then use browser Back and change a filter on the restored tab. Use browser Forward; inspect the selected dashboard tab.

While editing a filter, choose an input style such as Search box and then change its comparison operator. rootCause.explanation: restoreParameterMappingsIfNeeded replaces the edited parameter with parameterToRestore from dashboardBeforeEditing via setParamType. That full prior object includes the old widget settings, overwriting a widget-style change made earlier in the current unsaved edit.

reproductionPaths.explanation: While editing a dashboard filter, choose an unsaved input style such as Search box and then change its comparison operator. logicalBugs.explanation: A query filter restricts which rows are returned; its editor selects a column, a comparison and the values to compare. Enter a literal %, underscore or backslash in a text Contains, Does not contain, Starts with or Ends with filter. These characters are treated as pattern instructions instead of ordinary text, so rows can match without containing the entered character or be wrongly excluded; the same defect appears in graphical filters and SQL field-filter controls.

rootCause.explanation: SQL starts-with/contains/ends-with generate LIKE patterns by concatenating user values with wildcards without escaping literal %/_ or backslashes. This shared compiler serves notebook text filters and SQL field-filter operators, so literal-percent matching becomes wildcard matching.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Add a dashboard text filter using Starts with and connect it to a category column whose values do not begin with a percent sign. Apply a literal % as the filter value. The chart still displays all categories after refresh instead of no matches, treating the character as a wildcard rather than the text the user entered.

sourceBugs.name: A percent prefix matches categories that do not start with percent

reproductionPaths.expected: Starts with % should match category names beginning with the literal percent character. None of the four category names do, so the mapped card should show no results.
reproductionPaths.actual: The mapped card shows all four categories totaling 2,852. The % selection persists after refresh and the same nonmatching categories remain displayed.

Open the new filter, type % as its sole value, and apply.
Inspect the categories and total, then refresh.
