logicalBugs.explanation: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. A dashboard remembers the viewer’s previous filter choices, but opening it through a URL that only specifies a tab discards and overwrites those remembered choices. Selecting a tab unexpectedly resets independent filters even when the URL supplies no replacement values for them.

rootCause.explanation: getParameterValueFromQueryParams uses Object.keys(params).length > 0 to decide whether URL parameters exist. A tab query alone makes hasQueryParams true, so every absent filter falls back to its default instead of lastUsedValues.

reproductionPaths.explanation: A dashboard remembers the viewer’s previously used filter values. Open it through an address specifying only which tab to display, without giving replacement filter values. The remembered filters are cleared and that cleared state is saved for later visits, even though selecting a tab should not reset independent record restrictions.

sourceBugs.name: Opening a dashboard via a tab URL (?tab=...) discards and overwrites the user's last-used filter values

reproductionPaths.actual: URL becomes ...&date_range=&...&tab=1-overview and Date Range is empty. Afterwards GET /api/dashboard/1 last_used_param_values no longer has the date range entry (it was {"81cd957":"past3months",...} before).

logicalBugs.explanation: A date/time filter selects rows by a calendar date or an interval; the picker’s displayed dates and preview should describe the timestamps actually included. Type a fractional interval such as 0.5 into a relative-date picker and leave the field. The input can show 1 while its preview and applied filter use 5 units, so two simultaneously displayed controls disagree; this is different from an unsupported fraction that is visibly normalized consistently before applying.

rootCause.explanation: DateIntervalPicker uses NumberInputWithFallbackValue with decimal entry disabled. The component keeps a display string separately from the parent interval; transient fractional text followed by fallback-on-blur can leave displayed and applied numbers inconsistent. The precise fixture transaction ordering is inferred, rather than runtime-verified.

reproductionPaths.explanation: In a dashboard relative-date filter, type a fractional interval and leave the field. The numeric input normalizes to one unit while the preview and applied range still use a different multi-unit interval. This is contradictory simultaneous state, separately from an unsupported fraction consistently normalized everywhere before applying.

sourceBugs.name: Relative date preview disagrees with interval after blur

reproductionPaths.expected: The preview matches the interval displayed after validation: 1 previous month plus this month should cover September–October 2026. Invalid fractional input should not leave contradictory values.
reproductionPaths.actual: After blur, Interval displays 1 but the preview remains May 1–October 31, 2026.
reproSteps: Open an authenticated dashboard with a Date Range filter (for example a duplicate of E-commerce Insights).
Select Previous month, then reopen its Date Range editor.
Set interval to 2, enable Include this month and Update filter.
Reopen Date Range and replace Interval with 0.5 using normal typing.
Move focus away from Interval and compare its displayed value with the preview dates.

logicalBugs.explanation: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. Open a dashboard with filter values in its address, make an edit and save. The reload drops those URL values and restores older remembered selections instead, so text/heading cards can lose their filter and other cards can show earlier results despite the active selection before saving.

rootCause.explanation: After saving, updateDashboard calls fetchDashboard with queryParams:null and options.preserveParameters:false to clear editing state. This deliberately discards current parameter state and reinitializes from default/last-used values; the source comment documents a related race on slow networks.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Open a dashboard with active filter values in its address, including filters supplying variables in heading/text tiles. Make an unrelated dashboard content edit and save. The reload clears those selections or restores older remembered values, so previously substituted text and filtered charts no longer reflect the selection active before saving.

sourceBugs.name: Saving a dashboard edit replaces current filter values with stale remembered ones

reproductionPaths.expected: Saving dashboard layout/content changes preserves the currently applied filter values (as it does for filters connected to question columns); headings continue to show the substituted value.
reproductionPaths.actual: On dashboard 'QA Filter Reset C' with URL ?day=2026-10-25&word=hello&text=us-east, the headings read 'Day: On October 25, 2026' / 'Word: hello'. After Edit → add a heading → Save, the URL becomes ?day=&word=&text=us-east and headings show 'Day: {{dd}}' and 'Word: {{w}}'. The 'Text' filter (mapped to the Release requests Region column) kept us-east. Also seen on a dashboard where a Date filter was connected only to a heading (date=2026-10-25 → date=) and a required Region filter mapped to text/heading/SQL-variable cards reset to its default. In another run, saving a text-card edit replaced explicit URL filter values with older remembered ones.

Click the T (heading/text) dropdown > Heading and type 'Word: {{w}}'; click outside the card.
Click the filter icon (Add a filter or parameter) > Text or Category; set Label to 'Word'. On the heading card click 'Select…' and choose 'w'. Click Done, then Save.
In view mode open the Word filter, type 'hello' and apply it. Confirm the heading reads 'Word: hello' and the URL has ?word=hello.
Click the pencil (Edit dashboard), add another Heading (any text), click outside, and click Save.

Observe: the URL changes to ?word= , the Word filter widget is empty, and the heading shows 'Word: {{w}}' instead of 'Word: hello'. (Same with a Date picker filter connected only to a heading, e.g. 'Day: {{dd}}' with 2026-10-25.)

Move a dashboard to another collection and inspect its More info details immediately afterward. Its last-editor information still identifies the earlier edit until refresh instead of reflecting the completed move.

logicalBugs.explanation: A dashboard displays saved charts, tables and text as cards, optionally arranged in tabs; filter controls can update the cards connected to them. While a dashboard already has unsaved edits, press its “e” edit shortcut. It exits editing and drops the draft without a discard warning instead of preserving the active edit session.

rootCause.explanation: The dashboard keyboard shortcut toggles edit state regardless of isEditing/dirty state, invoking the cancel/discard path without a confirmation.

reproductionPaths.explanation: On a dashboard with unsaved editing changes, press its e shortcut while already in edit mode. The editor closes and the pending cards disappear without the discard confirmation offered by Cancel. Entering edit mode again shows the unchanged saved dashboard, confirming the draft was dropped rather than saved.

sourceBugs.name: Pressing 'e' in dashboard edit mode exits and silently discards all unsaved changes

reproductionPaths.expected: Pressing 'e' while already editing should do nothing. At minimum it should show the same 'Discard your changes?' confirmation that the Cancel button shows when there are unsaved changes.
reproductionPaths.actual: Edit mode closes right away and all unsaved cards disappear: the dashcard count went from 2 to 0 and the dashboard showed 'This dashboard is empty'. logicalBugs.explanation: Dashboard cards have visualization settings for chart type, colors, axes and number formatting; a custom click action can navigate to a URL or change dashboard filters. Apply a filter to a dashboard chart using a time-period comparison. Its comparison label displays a number followed by the literal word “undefined” instead of the intended time unit.

rootCause.explanation: Comparison period label generation indexes an unavailable temporal unit/period descriptor after filtered series normalization, interpolating undefined rather than a valid unit label.

reproductionPaths.explanation: On a dashboard number chart with a saved period comparison, apply a dashboard filter and inspect the comparison label. A label such as “4 quarters ago” becomes “4 undefined” instead of retaining the time unit. The data may remain visible, but the comparison description exposes an internal missing-value word.

sourceBugs.name: Dashboard comparison setting displays “4 undefined” after filtering

reproductionPaths.expected: The configured comparison remains labeled “4 quarters ago”, as it is with unfiltered dashboard data.
reproductionPaths.actual: The comparison button reads “4 undefined”. Reproduced on the original dashboard and its duplicate after reload.
reproSteps: Sign in and open /dashboard/1 (E-commerce Insights).
Set Date Range to Past 3 months and Product Category to Gizmo (equivalently open /dashboard/1?date_range=past3months&product_category=Gizmo).
Edit the dashboard, hover Revenue per quarter, and open Show visualization options.
On the Data tab, inspect the second comparison.
